# wifit3 > A standalone USB Wi-Fi auditor for Linux, Windows, and macOS.

> *At least* one of the [supported USB adapters](#supported-hardware) is **required**. ## Why? * **Cross-Platform:** Runs identically on Linux, macOS, and Windows. * **Wireless Driver Heaven:** Built-in wireless stack avoids kernel driver versioning hell and Windows' NDIS. * **Zero Runtime Dependencies:** No `aircrack-ng` or `reaver`, just pure Python with PyUSB & Textual libraries.

--- ## Features ### Reconnaissance & Analysis - **Multi-Card Aggregation:** Capture packets across multiple adapters simultaneously; pick a dedicated card to inject. - **Real-time Scanner:** 2.4GHz & 5GHz channel-hopping (split for multi-cards), DFS channels optional; tracks signal strength, encryption suites, WPA3/SAE transition modes; filter by channel and power. - **AP & Client Identification:** Fingerprints device vendors and categories; extracts router make and model from WPS beacons, chipset from vendor IEs; WPS M1 identity probe. - **Security Posture:** Detects WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise and PMF (skips attacks that can't work); flags Broadcom routers exposed to WPSplinter. - **Decloaking:** Reveals hidden SSIDs passively (BSSID siblings of visible networks) or actively; saves the SSIDs it finds. - **Packet Dashboard:** Visualizes real-time beacon, data, injection, and deauthentication packet rates. ### Attacks & Captures - **WPA/WPA2 Handshakes:** Passive sniffing and targeted deauthentication; validates crackable pairs; WPA1, PSK-SHA256 and FT-PSK (802.11r); exports `.pcap` and `.hc22000` files. - **PMKID Harvesting:** Active association harvest and passive sniffing for WPA/WPA2 PMKID key material (`.hc22000`). - **EvilTwin WPA3 Downgrade:** *(Experimental)* Clones the AP and evicts clients (via CSA, BTM, and de-auths) to capture handshakes. - **WPS Recovery Suite:** - **PixieDust:** Instant offline PIN recovery: *Null Secret*, *Static Secret*, and Ralink, RTL819x and eCos PRNG recovery. - **PushButton (PBC):** Detects physical WPS button presses and immediately extracts the plaintext WPA PSK. - **PIN Brute-Force:** Resumable WPS PIN cracking with known-PIN database and AP lock monitoring. - **WEP Suite:** Pure Python ARP replay, ChopChop, Fake Authentication, and PTW key recovery. ### Vault & Cracking - **Vault:** Shows every capture per AP, its PSK status (current, stale or uncracked); search, nicknames, add credentials by hand; `Show AP` and `Verify` against the live AP. - **Cracking:** Built-in CPU Crack, Hashcat (multiple wordlists; pause, resume, skip) and Hashtopolis; auto-crack after each capture; remembers which wordlists were tried. - **Wordlists:** Built-in default passwords, SSID variants, BSSID-based PSKs and probed SSIDs (also saved to a wordlist file). ## Screenshots | Scanner | Focus (single target) | |---|---| | | | | Vault (captures, keys and crackers) | |---| | | ## Supported Hardware > **Important:** *At least one supported USB wireless adapter is required.* | Chipset | Bands | Cards (Make + Model) | |---|---|---| | Atheros AR9271 | 2.4 GHz | ALFA AWUS036**NHA**, TP-Link TL-WN722N V1 | | MediaTek MT7601U | 2.4 GHz | Generic unbranded "nano" dongles | | MediaTek MT7610U | 2.4 / 5 GHz | ALFA AWUS036**ACHM**, Panda PAU0B | | MediaTek MT7612U | 2.4 / 5 GHz | ALFA AWUS036**ACM** | | MediaTek MT7921AU | 2.4 / 5 GHz | ALFA AWUS036**AXM[L]**, Panda PAU0F | | MediaTek MT7925U | 2.4 / 5 GHz | Netgear A9000 | | Realtek RTL8812AU | 2.4 / 5 GHz | ALFA AWUS036**ACH** | | Realtek RTL8814AU | 2.4 / 5 GHz | ALFA AWUS1900, ASUS USB-AC68 | | Realtek RTL8821AU | 2.4 / 5 GHz | ALFA AWUS036**ACS**, TP-Link Archer T2U Plus/Nano | | Realtek RTL8821CU | 2.4 / 5 GHz | Auscoumer 600 Mbps, Mercusys MU6H | | Realtek RTL8922AU | 2.4 / 5 GHz | ASUS USB-BE93 | | Realtek RTL8822BU | 2.4 / 5 GHz | TP-Link T3U Plus, Archer T4U v3 / T4U+ | | Realtek RTL8822CU | 2.4 / 5 GHz | D-Link AC13U | | Realtek RTL8187L/B | 2.4 GHz | ALFA AWUS036**H** | | Realtek RTL8188EUS | 2.4 GHz | TP-Link TL-WN722N v2/v3, Mercusys MW150US | | Realtek RTL8188FTV | 2.4 GHz | Generic unbranded dongles | | Realtek RTL8192CU | 2.4 GHz | TP-Link TL-WN823N v1 | | Realtek RTL8192FU | 2.4 GHz | D-Link AN3U rev. A1 | | Ralink RT2570 | 2.4 GHz | Buffalo Nintendo Wi-Fi USB Controller | | Ralink RT3070 | 2.4 GHz | ALFA AWUS036**NH**, TP-Link TL-WN7200ND | | Ralink RT5370 | 2.4 GHz | LOTEKOO 150 Mbps | | Ralink RT5372 | 2.4 GHz | Panda PAU05/PAU06 | | Ralink RT5572 | 2.4 / 5 GHz | Panda PAU09 N600 | Breakdown of each device's capabilities and limitations: [Supported Hardware Doc](docs/SUPPORTED-HARDWARE.md). ## Installation & Running ### Option 1: Download Prebuilt Binaries (Recommended) Download the latest standalone executable from [**Releases**](https://github.com/derv82/wifit3/releases/latest): * **Windows:** Download and run `wifit3-windows-x64.exe`. * **Linux x64 (non-sudo):** `chmod +x wifit3-linux-x64 && ./wifit3-linux-x64` * **Linux arm64 (non-sudo):** `chmod +x wifit3-linux-arm64 && ./wifit3-linux-arm64` * **macOS:** (bypass quarantine) ```bash xattr -d com.apple.quarantine wifit3-macos-universal2 chmod +x wifit3-macos-universal2 ./wifit3-macos-universal2 ``` ### Option 2: Run from Source wifit3 uses Astral's [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). `sync` sets up dependencies: ```bash uv sync uv run wifit3 ``` ### Option 3: Build your own binary ```bash uv run pyinstaller wifit3.spec --noconfirm --clean ``` Binary executable is written to `dist/` subdirectory. ### Android (Termux, no root) [@OliverRhyme](https://github.com/OliverRhyme) maintains [**wifit3-termux**](https://github.com/OliverRhyme/wifit3-termux), a native Termux port: no root, proot or VM. It uses `termux-usb` and asks Android for permission when a card is plugged in. Install steps are in its README. ## One-Time Driver Setup wifit3 automatically handles hardware configuration within the app, after clicking the `START` button: - **Linux:** Prompts once via `pkexec`/`sudo` to write udev permissions and blocklists in `/etc/modprobe.d/`. - **macOS:** No installation required; plug in the device and select *Allow* in the authorization dialog. - **Windows:** Prompts once via UAC to install WinUSB for the device. - **VirtualBox:** Add your device(s) to VirtualBox's `USB Filters` *before* plugging in. ## Uninstalling Return the previously-installed device to your operating system's Wi-Fi stack: 1. Select the card on the wifit3 splash screen. 2. Click the `Uninstall` button and confirm. 3. Accept the elevation prompt (UAC on Windows or `pkexec` on Linux). 4. Unplug and re-plug the adapter. On Linux, this deletes wifit3's `udev` and `modprobe` rules. On Windows, this uninstalls the WinUSB binding, and triggers a PnP device rescan (old driver reattaches). ## *Thank you, Linux!* wifit3 only exists because of the great people who reverse-engineered and maintained these Linux wireless drivers. It's usually a thankless job. Special thanks to: - **Christian "kimo" B. ([@kimocoder](https://github.com/kimocoder))** who maintains **wifite2** and `aircrack-ng`'s RTL8188EUS DKMS driver. - [**Neur0sp1cy**](https://github.com/neur0sp1cy): Close friend and the master to my Linux & wireless-hacking apprenticeship. - **Nick Morrow** ([@morrownr](https://github.com/morrownr)), legend, maintains the out-of-tree Realtek USB DKMS drivers. The full list is in **[CREDITS.md](docs/CREDITS.md)**. ## How it Works: Mini-Drivers wifit3 bypasses the operating system's native Wi-Fi stack entirely. It ships with lightweight Python ports of Linux kernel drivers ([src/wifit3/chips/\*](https://github.com/derv82/wifit3/tree/master/src/wifit3/chips)) that directly control wireless devices over USB bulk and control transfers. Because register-level frame injection and monitor mode are performed entirely in user space, Windows NDIS restrictions and Linux kernel driver locking do not apply. For how a driver is ported from the Linux source and checked against a USB capture of the Linux driver, see the [Porting Documentation](https://github.com/derv82/wifit3/blob/master/docs/porting/METHODOLOGY.md). ## License & Disclaimer **Code:** Licensed under [**GNU General Public License v2.0**](LICENSE) (matching upstream Linux drivers). **Firmware:** Vendor firmware blobs loaded onto adapters are redistributed verbatim under their respective manufacturers' licenses (details in [FIRMWARE.md](docs/FIRMWARE.md)). **⚠️ Notice & Disclaimer:** For use only on networks and equipment you own or are explicitly authorized to audit. wifit3 operates directly on USB hardware registers without kernel guardrails; use at your own risk.
readmeHtml:
wifit3

A standalone USB Wi-Fi auditor for Linux, Windows, and macOS.

At least one of the supported USB adapters is required.

Why?

  • Cross-Platform: Runs identically on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
  • Wireless Driver Heaven: Built-in wireless stack avoids kernel driver versioning hell and Windows' NDIS.
  • Zero Runtime Dependencies: No aircrack-ng or reaver, just pure Python with PyUSB & Textual libraries.

Features

Reconnaissance & Analysis

  • Multi-Card Aggregation: Capture packets across multiple adapters simultaneously; pick a dedicated card to inject.
  • Real-time Scanner: 2.4GHz & 5GHz channel-hopping (split for multi-cards), DFS channels optional; tracks signal strength, encryption suites, WPA3/SAE transition modes; filter by channel and power.
  • AP & Client Identification: Fingerprints device vendors and categories; extracts router make and model from WPS beacons, chipset from vendor IEs; WPS M1 identity probe.
  • Security Posture: Detects WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise and PMF (skips attacks that can't work); flags Broadcom routers exposed to WPSplinter.
  • Decloaking: Reveals hidden SSIDs passively (BSSID siblings of visible networks) or actively; saves the SSIDs it finds.
  • Packet Dashboard: Visualizes real-time beacon, data, injection, and deauthentication packet rates.

Attacks & Captures

  • WPA/WPA2 Handshakes: Passive sniffing and targeted deauthentication; validates crackable pairs; WPA1, PSK-SHA256 and FT-PSK (802.11r); exports .pcap and .hc22000 files.
  • PMKID Harvesting: Active association harvest and passive sniffing for WPA/WPA2 PMKID key material (.hc22000).
  • EvilTwin WPA3 Downgrade: (Experimental) Clones the AP and evicts clients (via CSA, BTM, and de-auths) to capture handshakes.
  • WPS Recovery Suite:
    • PixieDust: Instant offline PIN recovery: Null Secret, Static Secret, and Ralink, RTL819x and eCos PRNG recovery.
    • PushButton (PBC): Detects physical WPS button presses and immediately extracts the plaintext WPA PSK.
    • PIN Brute-Force: Resumable WPS PIN cracking with known-PIN database and AP lock monitoring.
  • WEP Suite: Pure Python ARP replay, ChopChop, Fake Authentication, and PTW key recovery.

Vault & Cracking

  • Vault: Shows every capture per AP, its PSK status (current, stale or uncracked); search, nicknames, add credentials by hand; Show AP and Verify against the live AP.
  • Cracking: Built-in CPU Crack, Hashcat (multiple wordlists; pause, resume, skip) and Hashtopolis; auto-crack after each capture; remembers which wordlists were tried.
  • Wordlists: Built-in default passwords, SSID variants, BSSID-based PSKs and probed SSIDs (also saved to a wordlist file).

Screenshots

Scanner Focus (single target)
Vault (captures, keys and crackers)

Supported Hardware

Important: At least one supported USB wireless adapter is required.

Chipset Bands Cards (Make + Model)
Atheros AR9271 2.4 GHz ALFA AWUS036NHA, TP-Link TL-WN722N V1
MediaTek MT7601U 2.4 GHz Generic unbranded "nano" dongles
MediaTek MT7610U 2.4 / 5 GHz ALFA AWUS036ACHM, Panda PAU0B
MediaTek MT7612U 2.4 / 5 GHz ALFA AWUS036ACM
MediaTek MT7921AU 2.4 / 5 GHz ALFA AWUS036AXM[L], Panda PAU0F
MediaTek MT7925U 2.4 / 5 GHz Netgear A9000
Realtek RTL8812AU 2.4 / 5 GHz ALFA AWUS036ACH
Realtek RTL8814AU 2.4 / 5 GHz ALFA AWUS1900, ASUS USB-AC68
Realtek RTL8821AU 2.4 / 5 GHz ALFA AWUS036ACS, TP-Link Archer T2U Plus/Nano
Realtek RTL8821CU 2.4 / 5 GHz Auscoumer 600 Mbps, Mercusys MU6H
Realtek RTL8922AU 2.4 / 5 GHz ASUS USB-BE93
Realtek RTL8822BU 2.4 / 5 GHz TP-Link T3U Plus, Archer T4U v3 / T4U+
Realtek RTL8822CU 2.4 / 5 GHz D-Link AC13U
Realtek RTL8187L/B 2.4 GHz ALFA AWUS036H
Realtek RTL8188EUS 2.4 GHz TP-Link TL-WN722N v2/v3, Mercusys MW150US
Realtek RTL8188FTV 2.4 GHz Generic unbranded dongles
Realtek RTL8192CU 2.4 GHz TP-Link TL-WN823N v1
Realtek RTL8192FU 2.4 GHz D-Link AN3U rev. A1
Ralink RT2570 2.4 GHz Buffalo Nintendo Wi-Fi USB Controller
Ralink RT3070 2.4 GHz ALFA AWUS036NH, TP-Link TL-WN7200ND
Ralink RT5370 2.4 GHz LOTEKOO 150 Mbps
Ralink RT5372 2.4 GHz Panda PAU05/PAU06
Ralink RT5572 2.4 / 5 GHz Panda PAU09 N600

Breakdown of each device's capabilities and limitations: Supported Hardware Doc.

Installation & Running

Option 1: Download Prebuilt Binaries (Recommended)

Download the latest standalone executable from Releases:

  • Windows: Download and run wifit3-windows-x64.exe.
  • Linux x64 (non-sudo): chmod +x wifit3-linux-x64 && ./wifit3-linux-x64
  • Linux arm64 (non-sudo): chmod +x wifit3-linux-arm64 && ./wifit3-linux-arm64
  • macOS: (bypass quarantine) 
    xattr -d com.apple.quarantine wifit3-macos-universal2
chmod +x wifit3-macos-universal2
./wifit3-macos-universal2

Option 2: Run from Source

wifit3 uses Astral's uv. sync sets up dependencies:

uv sync
uv run wifit3

Option 3: Build your own binary

uv run pyinstaller wifit3.spec --noconfirm --clean

Binary executable is written to dist/ subdirectory.

Android (Termux, no root)

@OliverRhyme maintains wifit3-termux, a native Termux port: no root, proot or VM. It uses termux-usb and asks Android for permission when a card is plugged in. Install steps are in its README.

One-Time Driver Setup

wifit3 automatically handles hardware configuration within the app, after clicking the START button:

  • Linux: Prompts once via pkexec/sudo to write udev permissions and blocklists in /etc/modprobe.d/.
  • macOS: No installation required; plug in the device and select Allow in the authorization dialog.
  • Windows: Prompts once via UAC to install WinUSB for the device.
  • VirtualBox: Add your device(s) to VirtualBox's USB Filters before plugging in.

Uninstalling

Return the previously-installed device to your operating system's Wi-Fi stack:

  1. Select the card on the wifit3 splash screen.
  2. Click the Uninstall button and confirm.
  3. Accept the elevation prompt (UAC on Windows or pkexec on Linux).
  4. Unplug and re-plug the adapter.

On Linux, this deletes wifit3's udev and modprobe rules. On Windows, this uninstalls the WinUSB binding, and triggers a PnP device rescan (old driver reattaches).

Thank you, Linux!

wifit3 only exists because of the great people who reverse-engineered and maintained these Linux wireless drivers. It's usually a thankless job.

Special thanks to:

  • Christian "kimo" B. (@kimocoder) who maintains wifite2 and aircrack-ng's RTL8188EUS DKMS driver.
  • Neur0sp1cy: Close friend and the master to my Linux & wireless-hacking apprenticeship.
  • Nick Morrow (@morrownr), legend, maintains the out-of-tree Realtek USB DKMS drivers.

The full list is in CREDITS.md.

How it Works: Mini-Drivers

wifit3 bypasses the operating system's native Wi-Fi stack entirely. It ships with lightweight Python ports of Linux kernel drivers (src/wifit3/chips/*) that directly control wireless devices over USB bulk and control transfers.

Because register-level frame injection and monitor mode are performed entirely in user space, Windows NDIS restrictions and Linux kernel driver locking do not apply.

For how a driver is ported from the Linux source and checked against a USB capture of the Linux driver, see the Porting Documentation.

License & Disclaimer

Code: Licensed under GNU General Public License v2.0 (matching upstream Linux drivers).

Firmware: Vendor firmware blobs loaded onto adapters are redistributed verbatim under their respective manufacturers' licenses (details in FIRMWARE.md).

⚠️ Notice & Disclaimer: For use only on networks and equipment you own or are explicitly authorized to audit. wifit3 operates directly on USB hardware registers without kernel guardrails; use at your own risk.

releases.body:
Sorry for the delay; we've been busy! ## Broadcom WPSplinter detection ([#136](https://github.com/derv82/wifit3/pull/136))

Focus's WPS probe button now also checks whether a router may be exposed to [WPSplinter](https://qkaiser.github.io/broadcom-wps/) (ported from [qkaiser/broadcom-wps](https://github.com/qkaiser/broadcom-wps)). releases.name: v0.6.0 (BETA)
releases.body: Pretty big release, big thanks to @xxcosita3czxx and @DensenDeluxe for bringing new features, usability, and correctness improvements across the board. ## Small terminals and phones | Scanner (Portrait) | Focus (Portrait) | |---|---| | | | - Condensed UI for smaller (60-column) terminals. - Art, sparklines, labels and buttons shrink or hide as the window gets smaller. - Looks good on NetHunter in portrait orientation. - Scanner: the SSID column shrinks to ensure client counts remain visible. - Vault: proper portrait mode (AP list above groups of captures). - Prefs, cracking and EvilTwin modals scroll on short screens. - Thanks @xxcosita3czxx for the detailed layout work in #114. ## Faster UI - No longer redraws and recomputes when nothing changed. - Tested on NetHunter (OnePlus 6T): ~19% more frames delivered, ~4% less CPU. - Thanks @xxcosita3czxx (#114

releases.name: v0.5.3 (BETA)
releases.body:
## Hashtopolis Support
- Uses Hashtopolis' User API (0.14.x and 1.0.x); submits job, polls for status, shows & stores any cracked PSKs.
- Thanks to @DensenDeluxe for their contributions in #90 

## Customizable Auto-Crack
- Select CPU cracker, Hashcat, or Hashtopolis to automatically run after each new capture (configured in Preferences).
- CPU Crack provides options to crack with wifit3's default wordlist, SSID variants, and/or probed SSIDs.
- Note: Cracking tool settings moved to `[cpu_crack]`/`[hashcat]`/`[hashtopolis]` tables in `config.toml`; existing settings migrate automatically.

## FT-PSK captures

- Captures `FT-PSK` (802.11r) handshakes and PMKIDs as hashcat `WPA*03/WPA*04` lines. Thanks @xxcosita3czxx in #113
- Cracking them needs a hashcat newer than 7.1.2; FT-PSKs are not sent to Hashtopolis.

## RTL8187L fixes, support RTL8187B
- Port-correctness fixes against the Linux driver. Noticeably better RF.
- Included support for the RTL8187B masquerading as RTL8187B for #116. *(Untested on hardware)*

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/derv82/wifit3/compare/v0.5.2...v0.5.3

releases.name: v0.5.2
releases.body:
Some important improvements after a night of debugging.

### EvilTwin fixes
- Answers a reassociation request with a reassociation response (Windows disconnected right after M1)
- (Re)association response carries the target's HT/VHT/HE/EHT/WMM details and a spec-correct AID, like hostapd
- A twin on its own BSSID (same channel) now records and saves its captures
- Resends M1 until the client's M2 arrives (up to 4 sends), like hostapd

### CPU Crack formats
- CPU Crack verifies WPA1 (key version 1) and PSK-SHA256 (key version 3, AES-CMAC) handshakes
- PSK-SHA256 PMKIDs are written for hashcat and no longer withheld as uncrackable

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/derv82/wifit3/compare/v0.5.1...v0.5.2

aiSummary.oneLiner: A standalone, cross-platform USB Wi-Fi auditor that aggregates packet captures without complex driver installations.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Wifit3 simplifies wireless security auditing by embedding a custom Wi-Fi driver stack directly into a Python application. This completely bypasses the notoriously difficult kernel driver setup on Linux and NDIS restrictions on Windows. It interfaces directly with supported USB Wi-Fi adapters via PyUSB, allowing users to capture packets and perform reconnaissance seamlessly across macOS, Linux, and Windows. It eliminates the need for legacy tools like aircrack-ng, providing a modern Terminal UI for analyzing wireless environments.
keyFeatures: User-space drivers: Bypasses OS kernel drivers to communicate directly with USB hardware, eliminating version conflicts.
Cross-platform parity: Functions identically on macOS, Windows, and Linux without requiring OS-specific configurations.
Zero dependencies: Operates purely in Python without relying on external C-based suites like aircrack-ng.
Multi-card aggregation: Combines packet captures from multiple connected Wi-Fi adapters to monitor wider spectrums.
Terminal UI: Provides a rich, responsive text-based interface built with the Textual library for easy navigation.

useCases.title: Cross-platform Auditing
useCases.description: Perform wireless security assessments from a macOS laptop without needing to boot into a specialized Linux VM.

useCases.title: Rapid Deployment
useCases.description: Deploy a Wi-Fi monitoring tool instantly on any machine with Python, avoiding complex kernel module compilation.

useCases.title: Environment Reconnaissance
useCases.description: Scan and log surrounding wireless networks, clients, and handshake packets across multiple channels simultaneously.

useCases.title: Hardware Integration
useCases.description: Quickly interface with off-the-shelf USB Wi-Fi dongles for custom packet capture scripts.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Security researchers, penetration testers, and network administrators. Requires a compatible USB Wi-Fi adapter and basic terminal skills.
